parts.title: Report Repair
parts.summary: Find the two entries in an expense report that sum to 2020 and multiply them together.
parts.algorithmSummary: Generalized sorted k-sum two-pointer search (k = 2 for Part 1, pre-built k = 3+ for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day01/shared/ (0.44 ms across 200 entries -> 355,875): immutable ExpenseReport with stable index preservation, exact BigInt product getter, bounded probe trace (kSumTrace.ts), interactive sorted-bar & sum-delta gauge visualizer, differentially verified against an independent brute-force oracle for k = 2 and k = 3.
parts.complexity: O(N log N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Generalizing sorted two-pointer search into recursive k-sum (kSum.ts) with an explicit ProbeObserver keeps Part 1 and Part 2 sharing one 100%-covered engine with zero Part 2 shared edits.
Checking !match rather than !product prevents false negatives when a valid tuple contains 0 (e.g., 0 + 2020 = 2020 has product 0n).

parts.title: Report Repair
parts.summary: Find the three distinct entries in an expense report that sum to 2020 and multiply them together.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day01/shared/ with k = 3 sorted anchor + converging two-pointer scan (0.52 ms across 200 entries -> 140,379,120): reuses findKSumTuple, bounded two-pass traceKSumSearch, and ExpenseRepairVisualizer with gold A1 anchor + L/R markers, differentially verified across 30 seeded PRNG fixtures against an independent O(N^3) all-valid-products brute-force oracle.
parts.complexity: O(N^2) time, O(N) space
learnings: Having a differential brute-force oracle return the full Set of all valid triple products avoids spurious mismatches on random fixtures that happen to contain multiple valid 2020 triples.
Pre-building generalized k-sum probing and A1/L/R visualizer tags in day01/shared/ let Part 2 land with zero shared edits.

parts.title: Password Philosophy
parts.summary: Count how many passwords in the corporate database contain their policy letter within the inclusive [min, max] occurrence range.
parts.algorithmSummary: Polymorphic PasswordValidationPolicy (SLED_RENTAL_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built TOBOGGAN_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day02/shared/ (1.63 ms across 1,000 entries -> 447): immutable PasswordEntry/PasswordDatabase, zero-derived-state SledEvaluation/TobogganEvaluation, single-pass bounded tracePasswordAudit, interactive character-strip visualizer, differentially verified against an independent split-count oracle across 40 seeded fixtures.
parts.complexity: O(N * L) time, O(N * L) space
learnings: Polymorphic PolicyEvaluation classes (SledEvaluation & TobogganEvaluation) storing only entry and policy eliminate both stored derived state and type-tag switches in PasswordStrip.tsx.
Doing a full linear scan instead of early-exiting on count > max keeps displayed occurrence counts and matched character highlights truthful in the visualizer with negligible runtime cost.

parts.title: Password Philosophy
parts.summary: Count how many passwords contain their policy letter at exactly one of the two 1-based positions.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day02/shared/ binding TOBOGGAN_POLICY into countValidPasswords, tracePasswordAudit, and PasswordAuditVisualizer (1.19 ms across 1,000 entries -> 249): O(1) 1-based positional XOR evaluation handling equal positions and out-of-bounds slots branch-free, differentially verified against an independent 1-based XOR oracle across 40 seeded fixtures.
parts.complexity: O(N * L) parse & storage, O(N) solve
learnings: Pre-building TOBOGGAN_POLICY with independent slot probes (matchedIndices.length === 1) handled first === second and out-of-bounds slots cleanly with zero Part 2 shared edits.
Explicitly testing extra unchecked occurrences and 0-based off-by-one traps guards against Part 1 count logic leaking into Part 2.

parts.title: Toboggan Trajectory
parts.summary: Count the trees encountered while descending a horizontally tiling forest grid along slope right 3, down 1 from the top-left corner.
parts.algorithmSummary: Modular-stride slope evaluator over shared/core Grid2D and euclideanMod in 2020/day03/shared/ with PART2_SLOPES pre-built for zero-churn Part 2 (1.22 ms across 323x31 forest -> 237): zero-derived-state LandingStep/TrajectoryRun/SlopeProgress models, synchronized row-by-row bounded traceTrajectories, HiDPI 3-panel canvas visualizer (wrapped tile, unwrapped corridor, minimap) resolving CSS tokens via getComputedStyle, differentially verified against an explicit string-tiling oracle.
parts.complexity: O(H * W) parse, O(H / down) solve, O(1) auxiliary solve space
learnings: Canvas 2D fillStyle/strokeStyle cannot parse var(--token) strings directly, so resolving light-mode CSS tokens once via getComputedStyle(canvas) keeps HiDPI canvas rendering theme-consistent.
Modeling LandingStep with primary fields only (stepIndex, slope, forestCols, isTree) and deriving row, col, wrappedCol, and tileRepeat via getters eliminates state drift.

parts.title: Toboggan Trajectory
parts.summary: Multiply the tree counts encountered across all five slopes (1,1), (3,1), (5,1), (7,1), and (1,2) on the horizontally repeating forest grid.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day03/shared/ binding PART2_SLOPES into createTobogganSolver and TobogganTrajectoryVisualizer (1.07 ms across 323x31 forest -> 2,106,818,610): exact BigInt 5-slope product, 5-slope focusable scoreboard & minimap canvas, differentially verified across 35 seeded PRNG grids (coprime/divisible widths and even/odd heights) against an explicit string-tiling oracle.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) parse, O(S * R) traversal time
learnings: Pre-building PART2_SLOPES and multi-slope synchronized tracing in day03/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 3 lines with zero shared-module edits.
Explicitly testing R = 2 ('#\n#' -> 0n) and crafted R = 3 zero-factor grids ensures down = 2 overshoot and zero-tree factors multiply cleanly in BigInt.

parts.title: Passport Processing
parts.summary: Count how many blank-line-separated passport records contain all seven required fields (byr, iyr, eyr, hgt, hcl, ecl, pid), treating cid as optional.
parts.algorithmSummary: Polymorphic PassportValidationPolicy (REQUIRED_FIELDS_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built STRICT_FIELD_POLICY & STRICT_FIELD_RULES for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day04/shared/ (1.78 ms across 255 passports -> 196): strict single-colon key:value parser rejecting fused/duplicate keys, zero-derived-state PresenceEvaluation/StrictFieldEvaluation/PassportTraceFrame, interactive 8-field passport card scanner visualizer, differentially verified against an independent whitespace-record set-inclusion oracle across 40 seeded batches.
parts.complexity: O(N * F) time, O(N * F) space
learnings: Enforcing a strict single-colon key:value grammar rejects malformed fused tokens like 'byr:1980ecl:brn' instead of silently capturing an invalid value.
Pre-building polymorphic STRICT_FIELD_RULES (including leading-zero-rejecting HeightRule) and STRICT_FIELD_POLICY in day04/shared/ prepares Part 2 with zero edits to shared/.

parts.title: Passport Processing
parts.summary: Count how many passports contain all seven required fields and satisfy strict per-field format and numeric range rules for byr, iyr, eyr, hgt, hcl, ecl, and pid.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day04/shared/ binding STRICT_FIELD_POLICY into countValidPassports, tracePassportScan, and PassportScanVisualizer (2.05 ms across ~253 passports -> 114): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, polymorphic YearRangeRule/HeightRule/PatternRule/AllowedValuesRule validation with per-field diagnostic feedback in PassportCard, differentially verified across 60 seeded synthetic passports against an independent standalone regex/numeric oracle.
parts.complexity: O(N * F) time, O(N * F) space
learnings: Pre-building STRICT_FIELD_RULES and STRICT_FIELD_POLICY in day04/shared/ allowed Part 2 to ship in ~22 LOC of domain code with zero edits to shared/ or part1/.
Generating ~50% guaranteed-valid and ~50% targeted-invalid synthetic passports avoids the (0.5)^7 zero-valid degeneracy trap in multi-field differential fuzzing.

parts.title: Binary Boarding
parts.summary: Decode 10-character binary space partitioning boarding passes ([FB]{7}[LR]{3}) into 10-bit seat IDs (row * 8 + col) and return the highest seat ID.
parts.algorithmSummary: Direct 10-bit binary seat decoding with flat Uint8Array(1024) CabinOccupancy and polymorphic SeatQueryPolicy (HIGHEST_SEAT_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built MISSING_INTERIOR_SEAT_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day05/shared/ (0.82 ms across 824 passes -> 878): non-circular iterative [lo, hi] BSP trace engine, single-SVG-path 128x8 horizontal cabin map + 10-bit BSP narrowing ribbon visualizer, exhaustively cross-verified across all 1,024 seat IDs plus 50 seeded PRNG manifests.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) manifest storage + O(1) 1 KB occupancy bitmap
learnings: Batching all occupied seats in a 128x8 airplane cabin into a single SVG <path> element keeps 60fps playback smooth without creating 1,024 DOM nodes.
Keeping traceSeatNarrowing(code: string) operating directly on raw F/B/L/R characters creates a genuinely non-circular exhaustive 1,024-seat differential oracle for bit-shift decoding.

parts.title: Binary Boarding
parts.summary: Find the unique unoccupied interior seat ID whose immediate adjacent seat IDs (-1 and +1) are both present on the boarding manifest.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day05/shared/ binding MISSING_INTERIOR_SEAT_POLICY into BoardingSolver and BoardingVisualizer (0.76 ms across 824 passes -> 504): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, scans fixed 1024-seat Uint8Array occupancy bitset across 1..1022 enforcing unique flanked gap, differentially verified across 50 seeded PRNG cabins (including duplicates, extreme interior gaps 1 and 1022, and multi-seat hole rejections) against two independent deduplicating oracles (sorted-adjacent-gap and arithmetic-series).
parts.complexity: O(N) parse & occupancy population, O(C) fixed 1024-seat scan
learnings: Pre-building MISSING_INTERIOR_SEAT_POLICY and CabinOccupancy.missingInteriorSeatIds in day05/shared/ let Part 2 ship in 4 lines of domain code with zero edits to shared/ or part1/.
Explicitly testing a 2-wide interior hole ([355, 356, 359, 360]) and deduplicating both differential oracles guarantees exact +1/-1 neighbor semantics even with duplicate passes.

parts.title: Custom Customs
parts.summary: Sum across blank-line-separated passenger groups the number of distinct questions (a-z) to which at least one group member answered yes.
parts.algorithmSummary: 26-bit integer bitmask encoding with branch-free Math.imul SWAR popcount26 and Template Method BitmaskConsensusPolicy (ANY_YES_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built ALL_YES_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day06/shared/ (1.89 ms across ~485 groups -> 6,748): single-pass CRLF/whitespace parser, bounded 80-frame trace, 26-column a-z CustomsMatrixSvg showing unanimous vs partial-only consensus strips, differentially verified across 50 seeded PRNG batches against an independent Set<string> union/intersection oracle.
parts.complexity: O(C) parse & O(P) solve time, O(P) retained space
learnings: Using Math.imul in a 32-bit SWAR popcount26 gives exact, branch-free O(1) bit counts over 26-bit masks with zero intermediate floating-point rounding.
Pre-building BOTH ANY_YES_POLICY and ALL_YES_POLICY under BitmaskConsensusPolicy with dual OR/AND strips in CustomsMatrixSvg prepares Part 2 with zero shared edits.

parts.title: Custom Customs
parts.summary: Sum across blank-line-separated passenger groups the number of questions (a-z) to which every member of the group answered yes.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day06/shared/ binding ALL_YES_POLICY into CustomsSolver and CustomsVisualizer (1.08 ms across ~466 groups -> 3,445): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, folds 26-bit declaration masks via bitwise AND with SWAR popcount26, CustomsMatrixSvg highlights the active AND consensus strip, differentially verified across 50 high-density seeded PRNG batches against an independent Set<string> intersection oracle plus P2 <= P1 monotonicity and non-trivial multi-person intersection checks.
parts.complexity: O(C) parse & O(P) solve time, O(P) retained space
learnings: Pre-building ALL_YES_POLICY and dual OR/AND strips in day06/shared/ let Part 2 ship in 3 lines of domain code with zero edits to shared/ or part1/.
Sampling high LCG bits at ~67% letter density in differential fuzzing prevents multi-person intersections from degenerating to all-zero and ensures non-trivial multi-person agreement is verified.

parts.title: Handy Haversacks
parts.summary: Count how many distinct outer bag colors can transitively contain at least one shiny gold bag under the weighted luggage containment rules.
parts.algorithmSummary: Unified LayeredBagQueryPolicy Template Method in 2020/day07/shared/ (ANCESTOR_COLORS_POLICY reverse-edge BFS for Part 1, pre-built NESTED_BAG_COUNT_POLICY Kahn topological longest-path rank + BigInt DP via shared/core/dag.ts for zero-churn Part 2; 9.76 ms across 594 bag rules -> 348): strict singular/plural parser, bounded layered SVG with lifted cubic Bezier skip-layer arcs and overflow summary pills, differentially verified across 35 seeded PRNG DAGs against independent reachability and recursive BigInt oracles.
parts.complexity: O(V + E) time, O(V + E) space
learnings: Validating that all referenced inner bag colors exist in BagRuleGraph before constructing shared/core DirectedGraph prevents silent sink synthesis.
Indexing all visible nodes across revealed layers in one nodeByColor map and lifting skip-layer Bezier curves proportionally to (toDepth - fromDepth - 1) keeps diamond DAG layouts crisp.

parts.title: Handy Haversacks
parts.summary: Calculate the total number of individual bags required inside a single shiny gold bag under the weighted luggage containment rules.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day07/shared/ binding NESTED_BAG_COUNT_POLICY into BagRuleSolver and HandyHaversacksVisualizer (9.31 ms across 594 bag rules -> 18,885): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, computes Kahn topological order and longest-path layer depth over shared/core DirectedGraph with bottom-up exact BigInt DP, differentially verified across 35 seeded PRNG DAGs (including deep multiplicative chains > Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) against an independent memoized DFS BigInt oracle.
parts.complexity: O(V + E) time, O(V + E) space
learnings: Pre-building NESTED_BAG_COUNT_POLICY and Kahn topological DP in day07/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 3 lines with zero edits to shared/ or part1/.
Testing deep multiplicative chains (> Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) and cyclic reachable subgraphs proves exact BigInt precision and cycle rejection at the Part 2 boundary.

parts.title: Handheld Halting
parts.summary: Execute a console's acc/jmp/nop boot code and return the accumulator value immediately before any instruction would execute a second time.
parts.algorithmSummary: Polymorphic InstructionOperation VM (acc/jmp/nop) with flat Uint8Array visited tracking and BootDiagnosisPolicy (LOOP_ACCUMULATOR_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built O(N) flat Int32Array reverse-BFS REPAIR_BOOT_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day08/shared/ (0.76 ms across 638 instructions -> 1,521): exact BigInt accumulator, zero-derived-state ExecutionStep/ExecutionRun/BootDiagnosis/BootTraceFrame using jmp<->nop involution, windowed monospace debugger + JumpArcSvg bezier gutter visualizer, differentially verified across 50 seeded PRNG programs against independent interpreter and O(N^2) brute-force repair oracles.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Modeling the boot code as a functional graph on 0..N makes the terminating set R an acyclic in-tree rooted at N, so reverse BFS via flat Int32Arrays runs in O(N) without an unreachable visited-guard V8 branch.
Advancing a monotonic applied-step cursor during downsampled traceBootDiagnosis guarantees accurate visitOrderAt(pc) history even when maxSteps compresses long runs.

parts.title: Handheld Halting
parts.summary: Identify the single corrupted jmp or nop instruction whose toggle makes the console boot code terminate cleanly at pc = length, and return the final accumulator.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day08/shared/ binding REPAIR_BOOT_POLICY into BootCodeSolver and BootDebuggerVisualizer (1.11 ms across 638 instructions -> 1,016): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, O(N) flat Int32Array reverse BFS from exit pc = N identifies the unique repairable instruction along the unpatched trajectory, gold patch-diff highlight & EXIT banner in BootDebuggerVisualizer, differentially verified across 40 seeded PRNG programs (checking both exact BigInt answer and patchedIndex) against an independent O(N^2) raw-string brute-force oracle.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Pre-building REPAIR_BOOT_POLICY and BootDebuggerVisualizer patch-diff badges in day08/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines with zero shared-module edits.
Testing > 2^53 accumulation via multiple safe-integer acc lines (9007199254740991 + 2) verifies BigInt accumulator precision without tripping BootInstruction's per-line safe-integer guard.

parts.title: Encoding Error
parts.summary: Find the first post-preamble number in an XMAS transmission that is not the sum of two distinct-valued numbers among the immediately preceding 25 numbers.
parts.algorithmSummary: Exact-BigInt sliding lastIndex map enforcing AoC's strict distinct-value (a != b) rule and pre-built O(N) half-open two-pointer ENCRYPTION_WEAKNESS_POLICY in 2020/day09/shared/ (1.07 ms across 1,000 numbers up to ~9.2e13 -> 18,272,118): zero-derived-state index-based models, discriminated union PreambleScanFrame | WeaknessScanFrame, bigintLog2-scaled SVG bar chart & pair-arc visualizer, differentially verified across 50 seeded PRNG streams each against independent O(W^2) pair and O(N^2) prefix-sum oracles.
parts.complexity: O(N * W) time, O(W) aux space
learnings: Tracking only lastIndex: Map<bigint, number> with conditional deletion (lastIndex.get(outVal) === windowStart) handles duplicate values cleanly without a redundant counts map, while left-to-right scanning guarantees p < q with zero swap branches.

Representing the Part 2 two-pointer window as half-open [windowStart, windowEnd) handles single-element > target drains to empty (windowStart === windowEnd, sum = 0n) without violating range invariants.

parts.title: Encoding Error
parts.summary: Find a contiguous range of at least two numbers in the XMAS transmission that sums to the Part 1 invalid number, and return the sum of its smallest and largest elements.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day09/shared/ binding ENCRYPTION_WEAKNESS_POLICY into XmasAttackSolver and XmasSignalVisualizer (1.52 ms across 1,000 numbers -> 2,186,361): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, O(N) half-open two-pointer sliding window in exact BigInt with two-phase preamble + weakness trace and green bracket/MIN/MAX markers in XmasSignalChart, differentially verified across 35 seeded PRNG streams (plus 3-element > 2^63 odd-bit BigInt and window-emptying traps) against an independent O(N * W^2) + O(N^2) prefix-sum oracle.
parts.complexity: O(N * W) total time (O(N) Part 2 search), O(N + W) space
learnings: Pre-building ENCRYPTION_WEAKNESS_POLICY, two-phase discriminated traces, and MIN/MAX SVG highlights in day09/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 7 lines with zero shared-module edits.
Using a 3-element contiguous range above 2^63 (so min + max != target) with odd low bits tests both exact BigInt summation and extrema extraction simultaneously.

parts.title: Adapter Array
parts.summary: Chain every joltage adapter in ascending order from outlet 0 to device max+3 and return the count of 1-jolt differences multiplied by the count of 3-jolt differences.
parts.algorithmSummary: Sorted AdapterChain scan with branchless JoltHistogram and pre-built O(N) sliding-3-predecessor exact-BigInt ArrangementTable DP in 2020/day10/shared/ (0.40 ms across 107 adapters -> 2,516): zero-derived-state models, O(1) shared ArrangementTable across trace frames, monotonic bigintLog2 ChainViewport with clipped Bezier jump arcs, light-mode AdapterChainChart SVG staircase visualizer, differentially verified across 30 seeded PRNG chains (plus explicit 2-jolt gaps and N=81 > 2^70 Tribonacci) against shared/core DirectedGraph.countPaths.
parts.complexity: O(N log N) sort, O(N) scan & DP, O(N) space
learnings: Sharing one frozen ArrangementTable across all ArrangementTraceFrames gives O(1) per-frame memory and lets ChainViewport compute exact maxWaysLog2 from frame.ways in O(1) by monotonicity.
Explicitly testing 2-jolt steps (absent from both official examples) and maxSlots = 2 clipped predecessor arcs ensures 100% V8 branch coverage and verifies general {1, 2, 3} gap handling.

parts.title: Adapter Array
parts.summary: Count the total number of distinct valid ways to arrange a subset of joltage adapters connecting the 0-jolt outlet to the built-in device with gaps of at most 3 jolts.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day10/shared/ binding ARRANGEMENT_COUNT_POLICY into AdapterArraySolver and AdapterChainVisualizer (0.46 ms across 107 adapters -> 296,196,766,695,424): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, O(N) sliding-3-predecessor exact-BigInt DP over sorted AdapterChain with O(1)-shared ArrangementTable trace frames and logarithmic jump-arc SVG visualization, differentially verified across 35 seeded PRNG shuffled chains (plus N=81 > 2^70 Tribonacci) against both top-down memoized DFS and shared/core DirectedGraph.countPaths.
parts.complexity: O(N log N) sort, O(N) DP, O(N) space
learnings: Pre-building ARRANGEMENT_COUNT_POLICY and logarithmic AdapterChainChart jump arcs in day10/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines with zero edits to shared/ or part1/.
Triple-oracle differential testing (DP vs top-down memoized DFS vs shared/core DirectedGraph.countPaths) on shuffled PRNG chains verifies exact BigInt counts independent of input order.

parts.title: Seating System
parts.summary: Simulate a rectangular ferry seating grid where empty seats fill with 0 occupied 8-neighbors and occupied seats vacate with >= 4 occupied 8-neighbors until equilibrium, returning final occupied seats.
parts.algorithmSummary: Precomputed CSR SeatGraph (Int32Array offsets/neighbors over non-floor seats) with double-buffered Uint8Array synchronous stepping, module-scoped TextDecoder('ascii') cycle detection, and polymorphic SeatingRule (ADJACENT_SEATING_RULE for Part 1, pre-built LINE_OF_SIGHT_SEATING_RULE for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day11/shared/ (16.56 ms across 97x97 grid -> 2,427): 2-pass bounded trace with unified diffSeatStates, HiDPI Canvas 2D SeatingCanvas with interactive hover/click neighbor-ray inspector, differentially verified across 30 seeded PRNG grids for both Part 1 and Part 2 against an independent 2D grid-scan oracle.
parts.complexity: O(R * C + T * E) time, O(R * C + S + E) space
learnings: Precomputing a static CSR neighbor graph over only non-floor seats eliminates all floor scans and sentinel branches in the cellular automaton hot loop.

Checking changes === 0 before cycle-set lookup prevents false cycle detection on equilibrium, while the 4x4 hollow-corner octagon deterministically triggers period-2 oscillation under Part 1's threshold.

parts.title: Seating System
parts.summary: Simulate the ferry seating grid using first-visible-seat line-of-sight along all 8 compass rays and a >= 5 occupied crowdedness threshold until equilibrium, returning final occupied seats.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day11/shared/ binding LINE_OF_SIGHT_SEATING_RULE (crowdThreshold = 5) into SeatingSystemSolver and SeatingVisualizer (41.07 ms across 97x98 grid -> 2,199): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, static CSR line-of-sight SeatGraph with HiDPI Canvas 2D golden ray inspector across floor corridors, differentially verified across AoC visibility/threshold edge fixtures (VIS_EIGHT, VIS_BLOCKED, VIS_ZERO, OCTAGON_4X4, SOLID_3X3) and 30 seeded PRNG grids against an independent 2D ray-scan oracle.
parts.complexity: O(S * max(R, C)) ray preprocessing + O(T * (S + E)) simulation, O(S + E) space
learnings: Pre-building LINE_OF_SIGHT_SEATING_RULE and golden ray overlays in day11/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines with zero shared-module edits.
No finite 2D layout can oscillate under Part 2's crowdThreshold = 5 because the topmost-leftmost seat in any hypothetical oscillating set can see at most 4 other oscillating seats (E, SW, S, SE).

parts.title: Rain Risk
parts.summary: Navigate a ferry from (0, 0) facing East through N/S/E/W/L/R/F steering instructions and return the Manhattan distance from the origin.
parts.algorithmSummary: Unified exact-BigInt (position, vector) state machine with exact 4-way quarter-turn rotation tuple and polymorphic NavigationRule (HEADING_NAVIGATION_RULE for Part 1, pre-built WAYPOINT_NAVIGATION_RULE for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day12/shared/ (1.34 ms across 783 instructions -> 439): zero-derived-state models, BigInt fixed-point aspect-preserving SVG projection safe past 2^1024, light-mode NauticalChartSvg course plot + compass/waypoint inset visualizer, differentially verified across official examples (25/286) and 50 seeded PRNG voyages for both Part 1 and Part 2 against an independent Gaussian-integer simulator.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) solve / O(min(N, maxSteps)) trace space
learnings: Unifying Part 1 heading and Part 2 waypoint under a single (position, vector) ShipState lets L, R, and F share 100% identical logic while isolating N/S/E/W behind a 1-method NavigationRule strategy.
Scaling BigInt coordinates in fixed-point before converting to Number and normalizing -0 branchlessly via (-ny / mag) + 0 keeps SVG projections finite and exact even for > 2^1024 coordinates.

parts.title: Rain Risk
parts.summary: Steer the ferry by shifting and rotating a relative waypoint starting at (10E, 1N), advancing forward in multiples of the waypoint vector, and returning the final Manhattan distance.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day12/shared/ binding WAYPOINT_NAVIGATION_RULE into RainRiskSolver and NavigationVisualizer (1.06 ms across 783 instructions -> 12,385): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, exact BigInt quarter-turn waypoint rotations around the ship with Waypoint Compass inset in NauticalChartSvg, differentially verified across the official example (286), zero-waypoint, odd-low-bit > 2^63 BigInt stress cases, multi-turn L/R invariance, and 40 seeded PRNG voyages against an independent Gaussian-integer simulator.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) solve / O(min(N, maxSteps)) trace space
learnings: Pre-building WAYPOINT_NAVIGATION_RULE and Waypoint Compass inset in day12/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines with zero shared-module edits.
Testing odd-low-bit > 2^63 BigInt moves after a 90-degree CW rotation verifies exact sign, scaling, and Manhattan accumulation with zero IEEE-754 rounding loss.

parts.title: Shuttle Search
parts.summary: Find the active shuttle bus departing earliest at or after the target timestamp and return its bus ID multiplied by the wait time in minutes.
parts.algorithmSummary: Exact-BigInt closed-form modular wait scan with polymorphic ShuttlePolicy (EARLIEST_BUS_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built CONSECUTIVE_ALIGNMENT_POLICY reusing read-only shared/core/crt.ts solveCongruences and bigintLog2 for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day13/shared/ (0.24 ms across 9 active buses -> 119): zero-derived-state EarliestBusFrame & CrtLockFrame, BigInt-scaled wait & log-modulus projections safe past 2^1024, light-mode SVG Departure Wait Timetable visualizer, differentially verified across all 6 official Part 2 examples and 30 seeded schedules against independent forward-scan and progressive-sieving oracles.
parts.complexity: O(K) Part 1 / O(K log M) Part 2 time, O(K) space
learnings: Reusing shared/core/crt.ts solveCongruences incrementally via acc = solveCongruences([acc, bus.congruence]) drives both Part 2 solving and step-by-step CRT modulus-locking traces with zero duplicated math.
Guarding finalModulus === 1n (returning 1 instead of bigintLog2(1n)/bigintLog2(1n) = 0/0) and maxWait === 0n keeps SVG wait/modulus projections NaN-free across degenerate schedules.

parts.title: Shuttle Search
parts.summary: Find the earliest timestamp t such that every active shuttle bus departs at t plus its 0-based index offset in the schedule.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day13/shared/ binding CONSECUTIVE_ALIGNMENT_POLICY (incremental BigInt CRT via read-only shared/core/crt.ts solveCongruences) into ShuttleSolver with a new light-mode SVG CRT Modulus-Locking Visualizer (0.41 ms across 9 active buses -> 1,106,724,616,194,525): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, log2-scaled horizontal locking bars keyed by 1-based frame step with compact BigInt suffixes, differentially verified across all 6 official AoC Part 2 examples, non-coprime compatible/incompatible schedules, > 2^64 BigInt primes, and 25 seeded distinct-prime schedules against an independent progressive-LCM-sieving oracle.
parts.complexity: O(K log M) time, O(K) space
learnings: Pre-building CONSECUTIVE_ALIGNMENT_POLICY and computePart2Rows(frames) in day13/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines and solved the 50-bit CRT alignment in 0.41 ms with zero shared edits.
Drawing distinct primes from a small pool for the progressive-LCM-sieving differential oracle guarantees pairwise coprimality and bounded per-step sieving, running all 25 randomized checks in 7 ms.

parts.title: Docking Data
parts.summary: Execute a 36-bit docking initialization program where each active bitmask overwrites 0 and 1 bits on written values while X passes bits through, and return the untruncated sum of all memory values.
parts.algorithmSummary: Exact 36-bit BigInt Bitmask (setMask & floatingMask without redundant keepMask) and sparse MemoryBank with O(1) running sum plus polymorphic DecoderChipPolicy (DECODER_V1_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built zero-alloc ascending submask generator DECODER_V2_POLICY with MAX_FLOATING_BITS=18 for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day14/shared/ (1.73 ms across 570 instructions -> 9,628,746,976,360): O(1) bounded MRU TraceMemoryBank, 36-bit MSB-to-LSB BitmaskGateSvg + MemoryLedgerPanels visualizer, differentially verified across official examples and 40 seeded PRNG programs for both v1 and v2 against independent 36-char binary-string oracles.
parts.complexity: O(N) Part 1 / O(sum 2^k_i) Part 2 time, O(U) space
learnings: In BigInt two's complement, (0n - 1n) & floatingMask wraps back to floatingMask; checking if (sub === 0n) return before decrementing keeps zero-alloc ascending submask enumeration termination-safe.
Maintaining an O(1) bounded MRU Map inside TraceMemoryBank avoids cloning tens of thousands of memory cells per trace frame in Part 2 while preserving exact newest-first register inspection.

parts.title: Docking Data
parts.summary: Execute the docking program under Decoder Chip v2 where mask 1 forces address bits to 1, 0 leaves address bits unchanged, and X floats across both 0 and 1, returning the untruncated memory sum.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day14/shared/ binding DECODER_V2_POLICY into DockingSolver and DockingVisualizer (19.34 ms across 570 instructions -> 4,574,598,714,592): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, zero-alloc ascending BigInt submask enumeration guarded by MAX_FLOATING_BITS=18 with gold floating-bit BitmaskGateSvg and capped MemoryLedgerPanels, differentially verified across the official example (208), MSB bit-35 masks, zero-clearing writes, a 131,073-write > 2^53 BigInt precision fixture, and 25 seeded PRNG programs against an independent 36-char binary-string expansion oracle.
parts.complexity: O(sum 2^f_i) time, O(U) sparse space
learnings: Pre-building DECODER_V2_POLICY, Bitmask.expandedAddresses, and gold floating-gate projection in day14/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines and solved 570 instructions (up to 512 addresses/write) in 19.34 ms with zero shared edits.
Using two disjoint writes totaling 2^17 + 1 = 131,073 cells of WORD_MASK hits the exact mathematical minimum for exceeding Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER with 36-bit cells while running in ~20 ms.

parts.title: Rambunctious Recitation
parts.summary: Play the Van Eck turn-age memory recitation game from a comma-separated starting sequence and return the 2,020th number spoken.
parts.algorithmSummary: Hybrid LastSeenTable (flat Uint32Array(targetTurn) storing 1-based last-spoken turns plus overflow Map for starting values >= targetTurn) using a uniform Commit-on-Speak exchange invariant with parameterized MemoryGameSolver(targetTurn) (PART1_TARGET_TURN = 2,020, pre-built PART2_TARGET_TURN = 30,000,000 with traceHorizon capped at 20,000 for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day15/shared/ (0.30 ms -> 492): dense-prefix + sampled trace turns, TurnArcTimelineSvg with in-window & off-window Bezier back-reference arcs + GrowthStatsPanel sparkline, differentially verified across all 7 official examples and 25 seeded sequences against an independent lastIndexOf reverse-scan oracle.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Every generated value after the starting sequence is strictly less than targetTurn, so a hybrid Uint32Array(targetTurn) + overflow Map delivers O(1) GC-free lookups while staying OOM-safe for arbitrary large starting seeds.

Applying the Commit-on-Speak invariant (exchange on every turn including seed turns) tracks duplicate starting numbers accurately in both solve() and trace() without special-case duplicate-seed branches.

parts.title: Rambunctious Recitation
parts.summary: Continue the Van Eck turn-age memory recitation game to the 30,000,000th turn and return the number spoken.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day15/shared/ binding PART2_TARGET_TURN (30,000,000) into MemoryGameSolver and MemoryGameVisualizer (579.27 ms -> 63,644): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, flat Uint32Array(30_000_000) + overflow Map with Commit-on-Speak exchange, responsive browser trace automatically capped at MAX_TRACE_TURN = 20,000 (200 sampled frames in < 5 ms), verified on the 30M official example (0,3,6 -> 175,594) and cross-checked across all 7 official seeds + edge seeds at horizons 50..5000 against an independent Store-Previous-Turn Map oracle.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) space for N = 30,000,000
learnings: Pre-building PART2_TARGET_TURN = 30_000_000, flat Uint32Array LastSeenTable, and MAX_TRACE_TURN = 20_000 horizon capping in day15/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines and kept browser playback instant with zero shared edits.
Adding Vitest { timeout: 15_000 } explicitly on the two 30M-turn tests avoids flaky 5000ms timeouts under V8 coverage on contended CI runners without slowing down normal local execution.

parts.title: Ticket Translation
parts.summary: Validate all nearby train ticket fields against the merged union of all field rule ranges and return the sum of every completely invalid value (ticket scanning error rate).
parts.algorithmSummary: BigInt-native ClosedInterval & IntervalUnion binary search (reusing read-only shared/core/interval.ts) paired with polymorphic TicketPolicy (ERROR_RATE_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built BigInt-bitmask degree-1 bipartite peeling DEPARTURE_PRODUCT_POLICY using shared/core bigintLog2 & bitCount for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day16/shared/ (1.98 ms across 237 nearby tickets -> 29,851): TicketScanResult.isValid tracks invalidIndices.length === 0 (immune to invalid-0 trap on personal input), SpectrumScannerSvg & PeelingMatrixSvg visualizer, differentially verified across official examples, invalid-0 traps, 56-field BigInt peeling, and 20 seeded random ticket sets against an independent linear-scan oracle.
parts.complexity: O(R log R + T * F log M) Part 1 / O(T * F^2 + F^2) Part 2 time, O(F + M) space
learnings: Personal input includes an invalid 0 on a nearby ticket while all rule lower bounds are >= 27; defining TicketScanResult.isValid as invalidIndices.length === 0 rather than invalidSum === 0n guarantees Part 2 discards it accurately.

Every finite bipartite compatibility graph with a unique perfect matching admits iterative degree-1 field peeling, and bigintLog2(1n << BigInt(k)) returns exact integer k for arbitrary field counts without 53-bit IEEE-754 limits.

parts.title: Ticket Translation
parts.summary: Discard invalid nearby tickets, deduce the unique mapping from rule names to ticket field positions, and return the product of the six 'departure' field values on your own ticket.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day16/shared/ binding DEPARTURE_PRODUCT_POLICY into TicketSolver and TicketTranslationVisualizer (8.66 ms across 20 fields and 237 nearby tickets -> 3,029,180,675,981): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, filters tickets via TicketScanResult.isValid (invalidIndices.length === 0), iteratively peels degree-1 BigInt compatibility masks via shared/core bigintLog2 and bitCount, renders PeelingMatrixSvg elimination trace, differentially verified across the official example, 6-prime > 2^99 BigInt exactness, invalid-0 trap tickets, and 25 seeded PRNG instances against an independent brute-force matrix-peeling oracle.
parts.complexity: O(T * F^2 + F^2) time, O(F^2) space
learnings: Pre-building DEPARTURE_PRODUCT_POLICY, BigInt compatibility bitmasks, and PeelingMatrixSvg in day16/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines with zero shared-module edits.
Testing six 6-digit primes producing a 100-bit BigInt product (~1.002e30 with odd LSB) proves exact arbitrary-precision departure multiplication without IEEE-754 loss.

parts.title: Conway Cubes
parts.summary: Simulate 6 simultaneous cycles of 3D Conway's Game of Life (26 neighbors) from an initial 2D slice at z = 0 and return the total number of active cubes.
parts.algorithmSummary: Separable 1D 3-tap box-sum convolution over 4 padded flat Uint8Array buffers with strictly growing active envelope B_t and polymorphic PocketPolicy (POCKET_3D_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built POCKET_4D_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day17/shared/ (1.75 ms across 8x8 seed -> 213 active cubes): zero buffer clears between cycles, exact 3D/4D parity selection (tmpA vs tmpB), free born/surviving/dying slice diffs via cur <-> next swap, HiDPI Canvas 2D SliceCardCanvas multi-slice strip + conditional 4D w-selector in ConwayCubesVisualizer, differentially verified against an independent sparse Set<string> Conway oracle across official examples (3D = 112, 4D = 848) and 16 seeded rectangular grids.
parts.complexity: O(d * sum_t V_t) time (9 reads/cell in 3D, 12 in 4D), O(V_padded) space
learnings: Overwriting all cells inside the strictly growing envelope B_t during each separable 1D box-sum pass guarantees exact global k-D box sums with zero buffer clears and zero stale border values across both 3D and 4D.
Swapping cur <-> next after transition retains exact S_{t-1} in next, enabling branchless born/surviving/dying diff-code extraction with zero extra buffer allocations.

parts.title: Conway Cubes
parts.summary: Simulate 6 simultaneous cycles of 4D Conway's Game of Life (80 Moore neighbors) from an initial 2D slice at (z = 0, w = 0) and return the total number of active hypercubes.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day17/shared/ binding POCKET_4D_POLICY into ConwayCubesSolver and ConwayCubesVisualizer (5.47 ms across 8x8 seed -> 1,624 active hypercubes): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, 4-pass separable 1D box-sum convolution over flat padded Uint8Array buffers with interactive w-hyperplane selector and HiDPI SliceCardCanvas diff cards, differentially verified cycle-by-cycle against an independent sparse 4D Set<string> 80-neighbor oracle on the official example (5 -> 29 -> 60 -> ... -> 848), w <-> -w and z <-> w slice symmetries across every cycle, edge seeds, and 16 seeded PRNG rectangular seeds.
parts.complexity: O(C * (W + 2C)(H + 2C)(1 + 2C)^2) time and space
learnings: Pre-building POCKET_4D_POLICY, 4-pass separable box-sum convolution, and the interactive HyperplaneSelector in day17/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 3 lines and solved 6 cycles of 4D Conway life in 5.47 ms with zero shared edits.

Explicitly verifying both w <-> -w mirror symmetry and z <-> w exchange symmetry across every trace frame provides an orthogonal structural invariant alongside sparse 80-neighbor differential testing.

parts.title: Operation Order
parts.summary: Evaluate arithmetic homework expressions containing +, *, and parentheses under equal left-to-right operator precedence and return the sum of all line values.
parts.algorithmSummary: Policy-parameterized iterative Pratt precedence-climbing parser producing frozen polymorphic BigInt Expression AST nodes (LiteralExpr, GroupExpr, BinaryExpr) with polymorphic PrecedencePolicy (EQUAL_PRECEDENCE_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built ADD_BEFORE_MUL_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day18/shared/ (3.83 ms across 376 expressions -> 4,491,283,311,856): zero switch chains, strict 16-case syntax validation, 2-pass range-skipping bounded traceHomework, leaf-midpoint scrollable AstTreeSvg + OperationOrderVisualizer playback, differentially verified across all 6 official Part 1 (26,457) and Part 2 (694,173) examples, > 2^64 BigInt overflow cases, and 60 seeded PRNG expressions against an independent Shunting-Yard two-stack evaluator.
parts.complexity: O(T) time, O(T) space for T total tokens
learnings: Parameterizing a Pratt precedence-climbing parser by a frozen PrecedencePolicy table lets Part 1 (+ = *) and Part 2 (+ > *) share 100% identical lexing, AST, evaluation, and SVG tree rendering with zero switch statements.

Computing leaf-midpoint x-coordinates in a scrollable light-mode SVG container guarantees zero node overlap even on 150-character nested expressions while keeping BigInt node badges readable via compact labels and exact tooltips.

parts.title: Operation Order
parts.summary: Evaluate arithmetic homework expressions where addition has higher precedence than multiplication (+ > *), left-associative with parenthesized grouping, and return the sum of all line values.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day18/shared/ binding ADD_BEFORE_MUL_POLICY into OperationOrderSolver and OperationOrderVisualizer (4.11 ms across 376 expressions -> 68,852,578,641,904): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, Pratt precedence-climbing parser with prec + 1 recursion evaluates addition clusters before multiplication in exact BigInt, leaf-midpoint AstTreeSvg renders deeper addition subtrees resolving under multiplication ancestors, differentially verified across all 6 official Part 2 examples (combined sum 694,173), > 2^68 BigInt precision tests, and 60 seeded PRNG expressions against an independent Shunting-Yard two-stack oracle.
parts.complexity: O(T) time, O(T) space for T total tokens
learnings: Pre-building ADD_BEFORE_MUL_POLICY (+ -> 2, * -> 1) and policy-keyed playback in day18/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines and evaluated 376 BigInt expressions in 4.11 ms with zero shared edits.
Giving the differential Shunting-Yard oracle its own independent local precedence table rather than reading solver.policy.precedence catches policy-wiring bugs as well as parser bugs.

parts.title: Monster Messages
parts.summary: Parse a context-free grammar of character and sequence rules and count how many received messages completely match start rule 0.
parts.algorithmSummary: General CFG-to-CNF compiler (right-binarization + cycle-safe BFS unit-rule closure + Left/LHS Int32Array CSR tables) driving a bit-31-safe Uint32Array bitset CYK recognizer with polymorphic GrammarPolicy (RAW_GRAMMAR_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built LOOP_PATCHED_GRAMMAR_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day19/shared/ (27.68 ms across 132 rules and 479 messages up to length 96 -> 265 matches): full-scan witness derivation span extractor (spans.ts), DPR-aware Canvas 2D CykTriangle + SpanRibbon + MonsterMessagesVisualizer playback, differentially verified across official Part 1 (2) and Part 2 (3 raw / 12 patched) examples, an independent 42^m 31^k block-matcher oracle, and 30 seeded random acyclic grammars against an independent regex oracle.
parts.complexity: O(L^3 * |G|) worst-case time, O(L^2 * ceil(V/32) + |G|) space
learnings: Right-binarizing k >= 3 productions before computing BFS reflexive-transitive unit-rule closure makes CYK handle arbitrary non-empty CFGs—including unit cycles, left/right/center recursion, and Part 2's looped rules 8 & 11—without hardcoding 42^m 31^n shortcuts.
Iterating active bitset symbols via lsb = bits & -bits and 31 - Math.clz32(lsb) with !== 0 checks stays 100% safe on JS bit 31 across multi-word Uint32Array CYK charts.

parts.title: Monster Messages
parts.summary: Replace rules 8 and 11 with recursive loop productions (8: 42 | 42 8 and 11: 42 31 | 42 11 31) and count how many received messages completely match start rule 0.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day19/shared/ binding LOOP_PATCHED_GRAMMAR_POLICY into MonsterMessagesSolver and MonsterMessagesVisualizer (82.40 ms across 132 rules and 479 messages -> 394 matches): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, general CFG-to-CNF compiler handles recursive rules 8 and 11 directly without fixed-width 42/31 assumptions, bit-31-safe Uint32Array bitset CYK chart with witness derivation span ribbon (rule42/rule31 roles) and DPR-aware CykTriangle playback, differentially verified across the official 31-rule / 15-message Part 2 example (12), 42^m 31^k boundary cases, variable-length/overlapping 42 & 31 rules, and 20 seeded grammars against an independent top-down memoized CFG oracle.
parts.complexity: O(L^3 * |G|) worst-case time, O(L^2 * ceil(V/32) + |G|) space
learnings: Pre-building LOOP_PATCHED_GRAMMAR_POLICY and general recursive CFG-to-CNF compilation in day19/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines and matched 394 messages in 82.40 ms with zero shared edits.
Because CNF unit-rule closure folds 8 -> 42 directly into rule 8, verifying span roles (rule42 and rule31 presence) rather than fixed span counts stays faithful to general recursive derivations.
